request.system:
Explain the result of an optimization model to someone who isn't an expert, in 3 to 5 sentences: what to do, what it achieves, and what limits it.

Use only the facts you're given: the decision values, the objective value, which constraints are binding (fully used), the slack in the others, and shadow prices if given (how much the objective changes per extra unit of a constraint's limit). Don't compute new numbers. Every number you write must appear in the facts, the model, or the problem, at most rounded.

content.text: Start 1 barista on Monday, 1 on Tuesday, 3 on Wednesday, 4 on Thursday, 3 on Friday, 4 on Saturday, and none on Sunday. This gives a total of 16 baristas, the fewest that still covers every day's minimum. Wednesday through Sunday are covered exactly at their minimums, so those days have no spare staff. Monday and Tuesday have surplus coverage of 2 and 1 baristas, respectively. The model doesn't give shadow prices, so it can't say how much the total would rise if a daily minimum increased.
